similarity panels route the query gate by cosine similarity to a blind-embedding slot centroid instead of decoding state.slots — baseline compositing only, no decoder mask to pair alpha with. scope=cell drops the datapoint competition entirely (see the slot-scope glossary below). All 9 cells (3 priors × 3 scopes) are complete, 5000/5000 steps. Exact values, every epoch logged:

All 40 cells complete, 10000/10000 steps. Base wins or ties alpha on query cross-entropy in every matched pair, and wins reconstruction NLL by four-plus orders of magnitude everywhere (∼0.44–0.51 vs ∼0.00001–0.0001) — alpha never closes this gap even at double the training. Binding stayed at chance throughout — purity == regime_base_rate exactly, in every cell, every epoch, both step counts.

KL(a‖alpha) is scope-dependent, and the direction flips by mixture: at scope=cell, every cell — alpha or base, any prior — sits flat at a tight 1.37–1.39 plateau from step 5000 straight through 10000; nothing moves. At scope=both/data, the two mixtures diverge in opposite directions with more training: every alpha cell’s KL drops substantially (e.g. mixed, alpha, decoder, both: 1.27→0.44), while base+blind_decoder keeps climbing at both scope for all three priors now that plain has finished too — final values plain 5.01, curriculum 4.44, mixed 2.43, all higher than their already-elevated step-5000 readings. So the compositing fix’s "one shared routing" property shows up only where the datapoint (feature-pooled) competition is active; the cell-only competition never engages it either way.

TabArena AUC mostly plateaus or drifts down past step 5000 — only base+decoder (mixed, curriculum) kept climbing to genuine new highs at 10000 (0.768, 0.764); every other family’s step-10000 value sits below its own step-4000/5000 peak, a real overfitting signal, not just noise.

Statistical check on the prior axis (repeated-measures ANOVA, 8 model families as blocks, step-5000 values): prior has a significant effect on TabArena AUC (F(2,14)=7.27, p=0.007) and query CE (F(2,14)=54.7, p<0.0001), driven specifically by plain differing from both mixed and curriculum (which are never significantly different from each other) — i.e. the evidence supports "some multiregime exposure beats none," not "more exposure is better." The two significant metrics point opposite directions: plain has the better (lower) overall query CE but the worse multiregime CE and TabArena AUC — consistent with plain being a specialist on the dominant regime it exclusively trains on. Restricted to vanilla alone (no slot mechanism, tested via its own per-fold TabArena variance instead of cross-family blocking), only plain vs curriculum clears significance (p=0.0015); plain vs mixed is borderline (p=0.071) and TabArena accuracy shows nothing significant at all — so the cross-family result is real but not independently confirmed by vanilla on its own, and shouldn’t be overstated as "multiregime prior is helpful" without that caveat.

Negative control (plain, decoder — complete): alpha led base on query CE through step 3500, but the gap crossed to favor base at step 4000 and stayed there through convergence (final: base 0.5318 vs alpha 0.5354). The same early-alpha-then-reversal shape appears in all three priors: alpha’s early advantage looks like a transient optimization effect rather than a regime-independent one, since it fades identically whether or not there is a regime to route between.

Matched vanilla, extended to 10000 steps (jobs 37003066 + 37018733): at 5000 steps every table-slot arm beat vanilla; by 10000 that stopped being universal — vanilla improved (or slot arms drifted down) enough that plain, alpha, blind_decoder (0.743 vs 0.745), curriculum, base, blind_decoder (0.751 vs 0.752), and curriculum, base, similarity, both (0.750 vs 0.752) are now at or slightly below matched vanilla. The slot mechanism still helps on average and in most cells, but "every arm beats vanilla" no longer holds at the longer training length — another instance of the same past-5000-steps drift seen in TabArena AUC generally.

Slot scope

Most cells on this page run slot_scope=cell_and_data; two blocks add the other two scopes on top of that default — blind_similarity (216–224) and the decoder/blind_decoder compositing block's own extension (228–243, job 37004859), both complete. scope selects which slot competition runs — and critically, an unused competition's parameters are dropped, not gated to zero: each scope is a separate model, so a comparison between them answers “does this competition help” rather than “did the extra parameters help.”

cell_and_data
the default; every panel above uses this
Runs both competitions. Cells within a row compete for feature slots first; the feature-mixed rows are then pooled and compete again for datapoint slots. Both feature_mix and row_mix convex gates exist and are readable above.
cell
219–221 (blind_similarity) and 228-231/236-239 (decoder/blind_decoder, job 37004859)
Only the feature-level competition runs; the datapoint (row) competition and its parameters are removed. The decoder still needs one distribution per row, so a row's assignment is the mean of its cells' assignments — still a valid distribution, since competitive attention already sums to one over slots for every cell.
data
222–224 (blind_similarity) and 232-235/240-243 (decoder/blind_decoder, job 37004859)
Only the row-level (datapoint) competition runs; the cell path is removed entirely. Rows are mean-pooled across features first, then compete for slots directly — the historical slot_backbone-style design, without the feature-level pass in front of it. This is the scope where baseline+blind_decoder's KL(a‖alpha) reproduces the same blow-up seen at cell_and_data — cell-only scope never shows it.

Vanilla nanoTabPFN — no slot mechanism at all

A plain NanoTabPFNModel, matched to the compositing block exactly on task, coherence, and TabArena breadth, now extended to 10000 steps like everything else on this page (jobs 37003066 + 37018733, all 15 tables). Most table-slot arms still beat this vanilla baseline on TabArena AUC, but not all -- three cells (plain/alpha/blind_decoder, curriculum/base/blind_decoder, curriculum/base/similarity/both) are now at or slightly below it; see the finding box above for the full breakdown.
